clauses.trace: Test 1 fails the changeset rm after the package writes and checks the tree snapshot is identical. Test 2 fails rename in pre mode and checks the snapshot, so the created pre dir is removed. Every test sets changelog:false, so a CHANGELOG.md the run created is never checked for removal on rollback.
err.cause is asserted toBe(boom) for the rm failure, and for the rename failure in test 2.

boundaries.boundary: failure after earlier package.json writes, with restore of changed and deleted files and removal of the created pre dir
a file the run created (a new CHANGELOG.md) is removed on rollback
a failure inside the changelog write after package.json was written

gap.missing: No apply-release-plan test enables changelog generation. Rollback of a CHANGELOG.md that did not exist before the run (restored to absence), and of an existing CHANGELOG.md that was rewritten, is never exercised.
gap.reproduction: In packages/apply-release-plan, use a real changelog generator (changelog not false). Start with pkg-a having no CHANGELOG.md and pkg-b with one. Make a later step fail (the changeset rm, or the pkg-b CHANGELOG write). Assert the tree snapshot equals the pre-run one: pkg-a/CHANGELOG.md absent, pkg-b/CHANGELOG.md in its previous bytes, and err.cause is the original error.

clauses.trace: At the first package.json write, seen[0] holds exactly one dot-prefixed file in .changeset. The journal exists before the first change (assertion at L268). It is named .apply-release-plan-journal.json (src/index.ts L96-L133).
No dot file remains in .changeset after a rollback (L269) or after a successful run (L277).
Latitude clause. A JSON journal with base64 file contents was chosen.

boundaries.boundary: journal exists before the first change
journal removed after success and after rollback

clauses.trace: version() calls getPackages(cwd), which reads the workspace package.json files, before recoverInterruptedRun runs. No test covers the order. The recovery test uses a valid package.json, so it would not notice a read that fails before recovery.
A journal and a half-applied state are set up. After version() the test asserts a warning containing 'interrupted' (L562), the journal is gone (L563), and the run completes.
After recovery the version is 1.1.0, so it was bumped once, and the changeset file is gone. Recovery of a created CHANGELOG.md or a created pre dir is not exercised.

boundaries.boundary: recovery runs before anything else is read, including a package.json truncated by the kill
restore after a kill plus rerun gives the uninterrupted result

gap.missing: recoverInterruptedRun runs after getPackages(cwd), so the CLI reads package files before looking for the journal. A run killed mid-write that leaves a package.json truncated or invalid makes version fail before recovery. No test covers this order.
gap.reproduction: Create a project with a valid journal whose files entry holds the original pkg-a package.json bytes. Overwrite packages/pkg-a/package.json with invalid JSON, such as '{ "name": "pkg-a", "ver'. Run version({cwd}). Expect it to restore the file, warn 'interrupted', remove the journal, and finish with pkg-a at 1.1.0 and the changeset consumed. Today getPackages throws first.

clauses.trace: CHANGELOG.md is made a directory so applyReleasePlan fails. The test asserts an ExitError with code 1 (L584-L585), log.error was called, and the printed text has no stack frames (L588).
The config has commit enabled and git.add and git.commit are mocked. Both are asserted not called after the failure.

boundaries.boundary: apply fails with commit enabled: exit 1, no stack trace, no git add or commit

clauses.trace: A successful version run bumps to 1.1.0, consumes the changeset and leaves no journal (version-no-journal.test.ts L480-L486). The existing index.test.ts and cli.test.ts suites run in the regression gates.

With a journal present, status writes the same plan as without one and the journal stays untouched. add --empty creates exactly one new .md, the journal stays untouched, and no 'interrupted' warning is printed.
